target: Invoicely, a local invoicing app with 6 planted authorization and session flaws
summary: The run executed live curl checks and confirmed 4 of the 6 planted flaws (IDOR on /api/invoices/101, open /api/admin/users, PATCH /api/me role escalation, open redirect) plus plaintext passwords, but never reported the weak session cookie or missing security headers, or the missing login rate limit, and did not fix or re-verify.
met: Ran authorization/abuse checks against the live local app with curl and showed request/response evidence (bob reads alice's invoice 101, alice reads /api/admin/users, bob PATCHes role to admin, redirect to evil.example)
Found the IDOR on /api/invoices/:id with the list-vs-direct-ID contrast
Found /api/admin/users open to any logged-in user and tied it to the UI-only hiding in public/index.html
Found the mass-assignment escalation on PATCH /api/me
Found the open redirect via /login?next= and the echo in /api/login
Found plaintext passwords stored and returned
Reported no invented flaws; all findings match ground truth
Gave a ranked fix-priority list with concrete fixes
missed: Did not report the session cookie lacking HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, even though login responses were captured with -i, and did not report missing security headers
Did not test or report the missing rate limit/lockout on POST /api/login
Did not apply fixes or rerun checks to prove them; it offered to do so instead (acceptable since not asked, but the rubric's re-verify item is unmet)
Summary claims every finding was executed and observed, but the final answer's headline framing omits that two of the six planted classes were never examined
skill_defects: The skill does not prompt a check of Set-Cookie flags and response security headers, though they were visible in captured -i output
The skill has no explicit brute-force/rate-limit probe step for the login endpoint (e.g., a loop of repeated bad logins)
The skill does not require a coverage checklist (authn/session, headers, redirects, rate limiting) before the final report, so whole categories were silently skipped
The skill does not say whether to apply fixes and re-verify or just recommend, leaving the proof-by-rerun step ambiguous
